title: The More We Get Rejected, the More We Succeed
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article reframes rejection as a necessary byproduct of taking chances rather than as a personal failure to avoid. It argues that the discomfort of being turned down should be redirected into a focus on the opportunity itself, since a portion of proposals will always fail and a portion will always succeed. The piece concludes that the best leaders actively seek more chances to be rejected because doing so is statistically the surest path to more eventual wins.
points: No one succeeds without experiencing a significant amount of rejection along the way.
Dwelling on the sting of rejection undermines confidence and discourages future risk-taking.
Good leaders reframe rejection as an inevitable cost of creating more chances to succeed, not as a personal dismissal.
The framing shift moves focus from the outcome of a single attempt to the volume of opportunities created.
Success is framed as a direct function of how many times someone is willing to risk being rejected.
quotes: Not everyone is going to like, buy, or accept what you promote. Rejection is inevitable.
Wallowing in the bitter taste of rejection simply undermines confidence and results in less risk-taking in the future.
They focus on the opportunity and the chance to compete instead of how much it stings.
They know the real lesson in rejection is not to do less, but to do more.
They view rejection as a necessary precursor to their success.
